status: frozen Task1 input; no product method implemented by S1

negotiation.unknownVersion: JSON-RPC error; remain standard-only for that capability
negotiation.peerWithoutExtensions: standard hello/report/ping.result/ping.tasks only; no fallback/SSH/PTY/config requirement; local configuration retained

boot_id.meaning: opaque kernel boot + counted interface-set epoch; equality, not a timestamp

iface.meaning: filter actually in force, empty = default; exact --iface grammar belongs to upstream collector

net_rx_total.parsing: raw decimal token -> BigInt/i64; public JSON remains numeric

net_tx_total.parsing: raw decimal token -> BigInt/i64; public JSON remains numeric

address.meaning: valid IPv4/IPv6 plus optional IPv6 zone; existing validSshAddress remains authoritative

target.meaning: existing validatePingNode/validExtraPingTarget; TCP host[:port], default80; ICMP host/address, no URL/shell syntax

methods.name: cf.report.batch
methods.semantics: Only frozen batch contributes CF resource history, traffic commit and probe denominators. Standard realtime report is latest/projection only for negotiated batch nodes. Sequence is one whole atomic batch, not a sample number. Reject gap/conflicting replay; ACK after durable acceptance, never just memory/WS send.

methods.name: cf.reporting.configure

revision.meaning: existing config MD5 identity, not authentication

interface.meaning: retain existing CF comma list/glob; each entry<=64; no shell/control characters

methods.semantics: Persist validated full persistent settings before result.persisted=true; temporary hint does not overwrite persistent config. No TerminalEnabled, AutoUpdate or credential field permitted. collect=0 remains explicit legacy-compatible sample-off setting, never used as idle default. CF default collect2/batch60; sampling continues while sending is idle. Traffic correction confirmation only after actual bounded correction. Local automatic update remains local policy, not a remote executable command.

methods.name: cf.ping.tasks
methods.semantics: Full per-node assigned list, numeric taskId maps persistently to immutable metricId generation. Byte-bounded without a64-task count cap. TCP and ICMP explicit. No same task in standard+CF schedules; negotiated CF task list owns schedule. Too-large config fails visibly, never truncates; accepted revision persisted before response.

methods.name: cf.ssh.events
methods.semantics: Preserve existing independent SSH stream/strictly increasing event sequence (gaps allowed due explicit queue/source gaps). Durable cursor+event policy capture/outbox only; does not assert external notification delivered. Returned high watermark scoped by server/tokenVersion/stream; <=max offered event. Empty status may ACK0. Payload excluded from public metrics/config/WS. Not resource batch ACK.

durableBatch.immutable: Freeze all params including clock/timestamps before first attempt; retry byte-identical params. Only RPC id may change to match new transport request. Same scope/sequence with different params is conflict, never last-write-wins.
durableBatch.ordering: Only next contiguous sequence or byte-identical durable replay accepted; gaps error with expectedSequence. Stream switch is explicit new-generation admission, not inferred from reconnect. Keep old receipts for admitted pending replay; token rotate invalidates old authority.
durableBatch.ackRange: accepted.from=accepted.to=request sequence; durableThrough is contiguous durable high watermark1..N (0 before any batch). Discard only frozen batches in this authenticated scope <=durableThrough and never beyond locally offered sequence. Success proves receipt plus recoverable facts/statistics effect survived eviction. S2 selects storage/atomic recovery; it must not change this meaning.
durableBatch.latest: Realtime report does not create duplicate history/probe/traffic entries; committed traffic baseline plus live projection shares one ledger.

fallback.authentication: same Bearer token and node ownership as WSS
fallback.eligibility: explicit CF origin and negotiated/configured fallback; same HTTPS origin, no cross-origin redirects, credentials/query or weaker legacy fallback
fallback.payload: same JSON-RPC cf.report.batch request; no legacy type/metrics body

durableBatch.streamAdmission: A first sequence1 batch for a new stream by the current authenticated node write lease explicitly admits it durably. Agent persists stream and frozen pending queue across restart; cannot switch while old batches lack durable ACK. Retain admitted old receipts; exact durable old replay may ACK its own scope but cannot retake new session ownership.

terminal.binary: private binary frames unchanged; max16384 bytes
terminal.credit: cf.terminal.credit maps legacy ack: cumulative bytes consumed, monotonic <=forwarded; forwarded-acked<=262144 per direction. Session/role comes from private socket attachment, not user-provided session routing. Not durable telemetry ACK.
terminal.disable: disabled retains operation/connection/generation/credentialVersion; send only after local config saved false and all PTYs/admission factories cleaned up. Broker checks exact pending disable binding even after server revoke; timeout remains localConfirmed=false.
terminal.privacy: No PTY bytes/ticket/token/SSH metadata in public snapshot, history, theme config, backup or logs.
terminal.negotiation: Private cf.terminal.hello(version1,protocol1,local capabilities) -> cf.terminal.bound(version1,current binding) bootstraps its own fixed v1 method set. No prior monitoring WSS/cf.capabilities required: HTTP reporting/schedule-inactive nodes retain independent terminal control. PTY group gates open/close/start/ready/resize/credit/exit/error/ping/pong; optional terminal.disable.v1 gates disable/disabled. Metadata capabilities do not grant permission.

errors.message: safe code only; request id paired; no response to notification; no credentials/raw payload echo
errors.privateTerminalInvalid: Unknown/wrong-role/malformed private terminal control closes its affected control/session as existing validator/broker does, with no JSON-RPC error response to a notification. Monitoring unknown notifications alone are ignored.
